newsitem.title: UK: Global first half M&A hits $654 billion - survey.
newsitem.headline: Global first half M&A hits $654 billion - survey.

text.p: World-wide mergers and acquisition (M&A) activity hit a record $654 billion in the first half of 1997, according to a study by Securities Data.
This outpaced a world-wide record of $575 billion in the second half of 1996, according to the study. The company statement did not give figures for the first half of 1996.
Overall M&A deals involving a European target maintained their share of global growth, with a first half rise of 2.3 percent to $157 billion.
Announced transactions involving a UK target in the first half of 1997, but not withdrawn, totalled $66.5 billion, an increase of 13 percent from the previous year.
Germany had a significant jump in M&A, Securities Data said, with $11.9 billion in the half year, a jump of 278 percent.

Goldman Sachs was the leading M&A advisor for completed or unconditional transactions with a European target in the first half of the year, with almost $21 billion from 15 deals. JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley placed second and third, respectively.

Among completed and unconditional UK target M&A deals, Schroder Group led with $11.5 billion in 13 deals. SBC Warburg SBVZ.S was second in the UK and Goldman Sachs came third. -- London newsroom +171 542 2734
